newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan, Bangladesh seek stronger ties.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan, Bangladesh seek stronger ties.

text.p: Pakistani and Bangladeshi foreign ministers held talks on Tuesday, and said they sought to strengthen relations damaged by diplomatic disagreements.

Bangladesh's Abdus Samad Azad and Pakistan's Gohar Ayub Khan held "wide-ranging discussions on matters of mutual interest, including bilateral and regional issues", said an official statement quoted by Pakistan's official APP news agency.

The meeting came several weeks after Islamabad rejected a Bangladeshi proposal for the creation of a sub-regional group with Pakistani's arch-rival India, as well as Nepal and Bhutan, within the seven-nation South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC).
Islamabad suspected the move could isolate it and said last month the new grouping could be formed only outside the SAARC and not within its framework.
A senior Bangladeshi official visited Pakistan last month hoping to ease the tensions but appeared to have failed to make much headway with the caretaker government then in office in Islamabad.

Bangladeshi sources said Dhaka's propoal was not aimed against Pakistan but at exploiting specific resources, such as river waters, with which only the countries of the sub-regional group were interested.

Azad's is the first high-level visit to Islamabad by a Bangladeshi official since new Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif took office on February 17 following his party's landslide victory in February 3 elections.

In Tuesday's talks, the two foreign ministers "expressed their desire to strengthen bilateral relations, which are sustained by a shared religion, history, traditions and culture," the official statement said.
They also "emphasised the need for identifying new areas for cooperation, especially in the economic, commercial and cultural fields".
The Pakistani minister "stressed that the private sectors in the two countries should be encouraged to enter into joint ventures", the statement said.
Azad also met Pakistan's new Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif and delivered a letter from Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, APP said.
Bangladesh constituted eastern Pakistan until its secession in December 1971 after the third India-Pakistan war, which New Delhi won.
